keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (-133..-129): the cities the page says Aristonicus seized 'in sea raids' (Leucae, Samos, Myndus, Colophon) and 'in the interior' (Thyatira, Apollonis), each drawn as a circle of 25-45 km; the page gives no extent beyond these places and dates the seizures only to 'before 130 BC'. Stratonicea on the Caicus, 'where Perperna first defeated him', is disputed. The shape is a minimum, not a boundary.

ledger.note: 133: Aristonicus raises the revolt. Attalus III 'bequeathed his kingdom to the Romans' in 133, exempting Pergamum and the Greek cities; Aristonicus, 'claiming to be an illegitimate son of Eumenes II', took the name Eumenes III and launched his revolt 'exploiting Rome's delay' (c. 133-129). He seized Leucae, Samos, Myndus and Colophon by sea and Thyatira and Apollonis inland, before 130.

region.text: the cities Aristonicus seized: Colophon, Leucae, Myndus and Samos on the coast, Thyatira and Apollonis inland

ledger.note: 129: the revolt ends. 'In 130 BC, Marcus Perperna replaced [Crassus Mucianus] and subdued Eumenes in their first encounter'; in 129 Eumenes 'was sent to Rome, paraded, and strangled in the Tullianum', after Perperna starved him into submission (the Pergamon page: a first Roman army was defeated in 131, a second force defeated him in 130). Manius Aquillius then divided the former Pergamene kingdom among Rome, Pontus and Cappadocia.

wars.outcome: Roman victory: Crassus Mucianus was defeated and killed after trying to retake Leucae, Perperna beat Aristonicus in 130 and he was strangled at Rome in 129; Ariarathes V of Cappadocia, Mithridates V of Pontus, Nicomedes II of Bithynia and Pylaemenes of Paphlagonia sided with Rome.
wars.note: The Pergamon page dates the first Roman defeat to 131 and Rome's annexation to 129.
